{'translation': '', 'source_text': "If you use an Apple Watch with cardio equipment, GymKit should be on your radar. It's the best way for your Apple Watch to exchange workout data with treadmills, ellipticals, and similar machines, resulting in more accurate measurements than either device could provide alone."}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': 'Apple launched GymKit back in 2017 with watchOS 4, but for years supported equipment was incredibly rare. The good news is that almost a decade later, you no longer have to spend around $15,000 to get a GymKit treadmill.'}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': "Instead, you can pick up a solid home treadmill with Apple Watch support for around $1,000. I've spent the entire summer testing the BowFlex T6 treadmill, which combines GymKit support, reasonable pricing, and dial-based controls, making it an easy recommendation."}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': 'Why Apple GymKit is so useful'}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': 'GymKit provides a two-way connection between your Apple Watch and compatible treadmills, ellipticals, steppers, and indoor bikes.'}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': 'Without GymKit, cardio equipment knows your pace and distance, but requires extra hardware to measure heart rate. The Apple Watch can record heart rate, but can only estimate distance and pace on a treadmill using wrist movement.'}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': 'GymKit lets both devices complement each other. The Apple Watch sends heart rate data to the treadmill, while the treadmill sends back its directly measured workout stats to the watch.'}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': 'Calories burned, speed, distance, pace, time, incline, and heart rate are all synced live between the treadmill and Apple Watch, creating a more unified, accurate record for the Fitness app, Anthony Winge, Director of Product Development at Johnson Health Tech, told 9to5Mac.'}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': 'Using the BowFlex T6 with GymKit'}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': "The pairing process is intentionally simple, but what impressed me was just how forgiving it is. You can connect the Apple Watch before you begin, but you don't have to follow a specific order."}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': 'For example, I can start a workout on the T6 console, get the belt moving, then tap my Apple Watch against the NFC reader to confirm the connection. Discovering that you can pair after starting a workout was genuinely a bit of an unlock for me. Starting on the treadmill first and adding the Apple Watch second feels more natural, somehow.'}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': "Once connected, the Apple Watch offers four GymKit workout options: Indoor Walk, Indoor Run, Time to Walk, and Time to Run. The first two are the standard Apple Watch workout experience, while the latter two let Apple Fitness+ subscribers combine the treadmill's GymKit data with Apple's audio-guided workouts."}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': 'After pairing, the treadmill and Apple Watch stay linked. Pause, resume, or end the workout on either side, and the other updates to match.'}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': 'Your heart rate is displayed on the treadmill console throughout the entire workout. As Winge mentioned, this is particularly useful for zone training, since you can monitor your heart rate without constantly looking at your wrist or grabbing the metal sensors on the treadmill.'}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': "BowFlex has added GymKit to its existing T6, T9, and T16 treadmill lineup. That means this feature isn't reserved only for the most expensive model."}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': 'iOS 27 brings GymKit to iPhone and AirPods Pro 3'}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': "Starting with iOS 27, GymKit is no longer limited to the Apple Watch. You can connect your iPhone to supported equipment and use AirPods Pro 3 as the heart rate source. I tested this experience with the BowFlex T6, and it's basically the GymKit experience without the Apple Watch."}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': "Meanwhile, watchOS 27 improves the wrist-based distance estimation during indoor walks and runs. It helps in situations where you don't have GymKit, but connecting directly to the treadmill is still the most accurate option."}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': 'Why GymKit has always been so hard to find'}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': 'The biggest issue with GymKit has always been availability.'}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': 'Initially, supported equipment was only available at upscale gyms in major cities. Equipment later expanded to venues in more regions, including some Planet Fitness locations, but support is still far from widespread. Even at participating gyms, you might find that only some of the machines are supported.'}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': "Buying GymKit equipment for a home gym was even harder. Last time I checked back in 2020, compatible Technogym treadmills started at around $14,000. That might make sense for a high-end commercial gym, but it's simply out of reach for most households."}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': 'At the time, I was hoping GymKit would eventually make its way down to treadmills in the $1,000 to $1,500 range. The BowFlex T6 fits right into that category.'}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': 'BowFlex T6 brings GymKit home'}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': 'The BowFlex T6 treadmill is priced at $999 (originally $1,299).'}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': "For a decent home treadmill, that's a reasonable price, roughly one-tenth of the last GymKit model I came across."}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': "Rather than an expensive built-in touchscreen, the T6 uses a simple, straightforward console paired with an adjustable shelf for placing your own iPad, tablet, or phone. This way, you're free to choose your workout platform rather than being locked into a single service."}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': "You can use Apple Fitness+ (Apple One Premier), Peloton, Zwift, or BowFlex's optional JRNY platform. Your device can connect via the T6's built-in Bluetooth speakers, while the console continues to display the workout metrics you need."}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': "The treadmill itself doesn't require a monthly fee. In an era where connected fitness equipment often charges extra for even the most basic features, that distinction matters."}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': 'Dial-based controls are a surprisingly delightful highlight'}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': 'Beyond GymKit and the reasonable price, my favorite feature is how the BowFlex T6 handles speed and incline changes.'}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': 'Instead of fumbling with buttons while walking or running, you simply turn the dials mounted on the handlebars. The right dial adjusts speed, while the left dial controls incline. I found this method to be faster and more intuitive to adjust.'}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': 'BowFlex pairs these QuickDial controls with what they call the MaxReact drive system, which responds quickly when you change speed or incline. This makes the controls especially handy for interval workouts where you need to frequently shift intensity.'}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': "My first experience with dial-based controls like these came years ago when I tested Peloton's original treadmill. That machine was astronomically priced, so finding a similar control system on a far more affordable treadmill is a definite plus."}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': 'The T6 also features a 20-inch by 60-inch cushioned running deck, a top speed of 12 mph, up to 15% powered incline, a three-speed fan, and a foldable running deck. These are solid basics for a home treadmill, without forcing you to commit to a large touchscreen.'}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': 'Wrap-up'}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': "Overall, I strongly recommend the BowFlex T6 treadmill for anyone looking to build a home gym on a limited budget. BowFlex offers pricier models with advanced displays and larger running decks, but the T6 delivers on the key points without adding costs I don't need."}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': 'The GymKit experience with Apple Watch has always been excellent, and it recently expanded to include iPhone and AirPods Pro 3. If you use a Samsung Galaxy Watch, this treadmill supports that too.'}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': 'Have you used an Apple Watch with Apple GymKit before? Share your thoughts in the comments.'}

{'translation': '', 'source_text': 'Get the most out of your Apple devices'}
